runs.complete_norm_class_proof: For primitive r, q(r) divides 2I(r), with I(r)=(-2*theta*x,y1,...,y4). Away from the inert prime (2), I(r) is locally O. At (2), either a spatial coordinate is a unit, giving v_2(q)<=1, or x is a unit and every yi lies in (2), in which case q=-2*theta*x^2 mod (4), so v_2(q)=1. Therefore (q) is (1) or (2).

For primitive r, q(r) divides 2I(r), with I(r)=(-delta*theta*x,y1,...,y4). At p=(delta), either a spatial coordinate is a unit, giving v_p(q)=0, or x is a unit and all yi lie in p, giving q=-delta*theta*x^2 mod p^2 and v_p(q)=1. Away from p and the inert prime (2), I(r) is locally O; at (2), v_2(q)<=1. Therefore (q) is one of (1),(2),(delta),(2*delta).
